report.summary: Metrics module: per-file health metrics with comment-aware counting, lizard integration, and guard detection.
risks: _count_comments | medium | Block comment detection uses simple string-in-line checks, may miscount multi-line block comments that span multiple lines without block end marker on same line. | Review block comment logic for languages with nested or multi-line block comments.
_lizard_cc | low | Catches all exceptions silently, returns None; may hide import or analysis errors. | Add specific exception handling or logging.

handoff.purpose: Compute per-file health metrics: LOC, function count, comment density, guard density, long functions, and optional cyclomatic complexity via lizard.

symbols.name: _LONG_FN
symbols.note: Threshold for long function flag, set to 60 lines.

symbols.name: lizard_available
symbols.note: Returns True if lizard module can be imported, else False. Cached with maxsize=1.

symbols.name: file_metrics
symbols.note: Main entry point: returns dict with language, loc, n_functions, comment_density, guard_density, guard_count, long_functions, and optionally cc_avg/cc_max.

symbols.name: _count_comments
symbols.note: Counts comment lines for Python using tokenize, for other languages using line/block comment delimiters from LanguageSpec.

symbols.name: _count_guards
symbols.note: Counts occurrences of guard keywords from LanguageSpec using regex for alphabetic keywords, else simple count.

symbols.name: _lizard_cc
symbols.note: If lizard available, computes average and max cyclomatic complexity from analysis; returns None on failure or no functions.

claims.text: Stdlib-only baseline (LOC, function count, comment density, guard/over-defensive density, long-function flag).
claims.why: file_metrics computes loc, n_functions, comment_density, guard_density, guard_count, long_functions using only stdlib and internal modules.

claims.text: If ``lizard`` is installed, real cyclomatic complexity (avg/max) is added for the languages lizard supports.
claims.why: lizard_available() checks import; _lizard_cc() computes cc_avg and cc_max if lizard is available and analysis succeeds.

claims.text: Per-file health metrics — the 'code health' signal, comment-aware per language.
claims.why: file_metrics returns a dict with health metrics; comment counting is language-aware via LanguageSpec.

observations.what: file_metrics uses lizard_available() which is cached; if lizard is not available, cc is None and no lizard metrics are added.

_count_comments for Python uses tokenize which is accurate; for other languages it uses simple string matching which may miscount block comments that span multiple lines without block end marker on the same line.
_count_guards uses re.findall for alphabetic keywords, which could match inside identifiers or strings; for non-alpha keywords uses simple count which could also match inside strings.
_lizard_cc catches all exceptions silently, returning None; this may hide import errors or analysis failures.
The constant _LONG_FN is set to 60, used as threshold for flagging long functions.
